items.stem: What does the first principal component in PCA capture?

options.text: The direction of greatest variance in the data
options.rationale: Correct: PC1 is the maximum-variance direction.

options.text: A random axis in the data
options.rationale: Components are chosen to maximise variance, not randomly.

items.stem: Which TWO cautions apply when reading a t-SNE plot? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Distances between clusters may not be meaningful
options.rationale: Correct: t-SNE does not preserve global distances well.

options.text: Cluster sizes can be distorted by the method
options.rationale: Correct: apparent sizes are not reliable.

options.text: The axes have fixed real-world units
options.rationale: t-SNE axes have no inherent units.

options.text: It always preserves exact global geometry

items.explanation: Correct: t-SNE does not preserve global distances well.

items.stem: How should you choose the number of PCA components to keep?

options.text: Keep enough to explain a target share of total variance
options.rationale: Correct: explained-variance thresholds guide the choice.
Two is only for 2-D plotting, not a general rule.

options.text: Keep the components explaining the least variance
Keep as many as there are rows
